channel.title: Use & Like: app news
channel.description: What changed in the apps you use, in our own words, with what it means for you and what to do about it.

item.title: 10 new graphic design apps climbing the App Store this week
item.description: Ten design and drawing apps released in the last 60 days rose into the US App Store's Graphics & Design charts this week, from the 3D renderer RAYS to Wallmix's wallpapers and widgets.

item.title: 10 new music apps climbing the App Store this week
item.description: These music apps came out in the last 60 days and rose into the US App Store's Music charts this week, from chord and synth instruments to metronomes and retro music players for your Apple Music library.

item.title: 10 new photo and video apps climbing the App Store this week
item.description: These photo and video apps came out in the last 60 days and rose into the US App Store's Photo & Video charts this week, from RAW editors and film looks to a photo booth and a camera trick that gets kids to look at the lens.

item.title: 10 new productivity apps climbing the App Store this week
item.description: These productivity apps came out in the last 60 days and rose into the US App Store's Productivity charts this week, from a 3D CAD app to focus timers, planners and a family chore chart.

item.title: 10 new weather apps for iPhone climbing the App Store this week
item.description: Ten weather apps that came out in the last 60 days rose into the US App Store's Weather charts this week, from Snow Day Radar's snow day odds to SkyWX's radar and alerts.

item.title: 6 new education apps climbing the App Store this week
item.description: Six learning apps released in the last 60 days rose into the US App Store's Education charts this week, from the CrowCards flashcards to a plant explorer.

item.title: 7 new navigation and GPS apps climbing the App Store this week
item.description: Seven navigation apps released in the last 60 days rose into the US App Store's Navigation charts this week, from a trail ride tracker to a speed camera warner.

item.title: 7 new travel apps for iPhone climbing the App Store this week
item.description: Seven travel apps released in the last 60 days rose into the US App Store's Travel charts this week, from Watchmen's camera map to an offline voice translator.

item.title: 8 new entertainment apps for iPhone climbing the App Store this week
item.description: Eight entertainment apps released in the last 60 days rose into the US App Store's Entertainment charts this week, including Jitless for PC games and Roku's new official app.

item.title: 8 new utility apps climbing the App Store this week
item.description: These utility apps came out in the last 60 days and rose into the US App Store's Utilities charts this week, most of them made for the foldable iPhone Duo, from Safari extensions to desk clocks and a fold counter.

item.title: 9 new health and fitness apps climbing the App Store this week
item.description: These health and fitness apps came out in the last 60 days and rose into the US App Store's Health & Fitness charts this week, from lifting logs and a calorie tracker to Apple Watch tools for naps, counting and blood oxygen.

item.title: 9 new lifestyle apps climbing the App Store this week
item.description: These lifestyle apps came out in the last 60 days and rose into the US App Store's Lifestyle charts this week, from a retro fridge wallpaper to a phone lock for nights out.

item.title: Budget apps that connect to your bank vs offline trackers explained
item.description: A budget app either reads your bank and card transactions through a link, as Gemini now can through Google Wallet, or works only with what you type in, and that choice decides how much it sees, where your numbers are stored and what you give up in return.

item.title: Copper landline switch off: what replaces your home phone and alarm
item.description: AT&T and Verizon have started switching off old copper landlines area by area, and their replacements keep your number but run on home power with a backup battery, so alarms, medical alert devices and cordless phones need a check before your date.

item.title: Gemini models explained: Flash-Lite, Hydrogen, Pro, Argon and Carbon
item.description: The Gemini app now lists five models, and which ones you can pick depends on your plan: without a Google AI plan you get Auto or Flash-Lite, AI Plus adds Hydrogen, AI Pro adds Pro and Argon, and only AI Ultra gets Carbon.

item.title: Roku app for iPhone: free movies and live TV with no account
item.description: Roku has put out a new app, Roku App (Official), for watching free movies, shows and more than 500 live TV channels on iPhone and iPad without an account, subscription or credit card. It came out on 10 November and was #73 among free Entertainment apps on the US App Store on 15 November.

item.title: AI agents shopping for you: what ChatGPT, Gemini and Meta Muse can do
item.description: Since this week, ChatGPT's Dots agents can buy things for US Pro subscribers once you approve each purchase, Meta's Muse can phone US businesses for paying users, and Gemini can read your Google Wallet spending without touching your money; some sellers, Amazon and United Airlines among them, block agents.

item.title: Apple smart glasses rumors: Siri, iPhone apps and a 2027 release
item.description: Apple's first smart glasses would be run by Siri using built-in cameras, with no display, according to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman as reported by MacRumors. Apple hasn't announced them; the report points to a WWDC unveiling in June 2027 and shipping later that year.

item.title: Apple Watch piano app Fingertip Instruments plays a tune as you tap
item.description: Fingertip Instruments is a new 99-cent app: you write a melody on your iPhone, send it to your Apple Watch and play it one note at a time by tapping your fingers. It came out on 14 November and was #24 in paid Music apps on the US App Store the next day.

item.title: Coloring with Farah: coloring book app for kids and adults on iPad
item.description: Coloring with Farah is a new coloring app with seven picture-led story books and 127 pages for a one-time $9.99, no subscription. It was #31 among paid Graphics & Design apps on the US App Store on 15 November.

item.title: Duo Holy Bible app opens like a printed book on the iPhone Duo
item.description: Duo Holy Bible is a new $4.99 King James Bible app built for the folding iPhone Duo: unfold the phone and the book opens to a two-page spread, fold it and the book closes. It was #52 in paid Reference apps on the US App Store on 15 November.

item.title: eniwher3 is a free online scratch pad for notes and to-dos
item.description: eniwher3 is a new free scratch pad that runs in any browser: double-click empty space or paste to drop a note, then drag it anywhere on the board. Sign in with your email and the board syncs between your laptop and phone.

item.title: Face Witness face maker app lets you build a face piece by piece
item.description: Face Witness is a new 99-cent iPhone app for building a face from separate parts: you pick eyes, a nose, a mouth, hair and other details, then move and resize each one. It was #4 in paid Entertainment apps on the US App Store on 15 November.

item.title: iPhone charger watts explained: what iPhone, iPad and Mac need
item.description: Depending on the model, an iPhone needs a USB-C adapter of 18 to 60 watts to fast charge, and Apple says a Mac charges from any USB Power Delivery adapter, even one with fewer watts than recommended, so one strong enough USB-C adapter can charge several of your devices, though not always at full speed.

item.title: iPhone Duo computer mode: DuoMiniMac adds a desktop and trackpad
item.description: DuoMiniMac is a new $4.99 app that turns the unfolded iPhone Duo into a small laptop-style desktop, with windows, a menu bar and a Dock on the top half and a keyboard and trackpad on the bottom half. It was #97 in paid Utilities apps on the US App Store on 15 November.

item.title: Local Video Upscaler: AI video upscaler app for iPhone and Mac works offline
item.description: Local Video Upscaler is a $9.99 app that sharpens old or low-resolution videos to HD or 4K on your iPhone, iPad or Mac, without uploading them anywhere. It was #67 among paid Photo & Video apps on the US App Store on 15 November.

item.title: LyricsNow: free synced lyrics app for Apple Music and Spotify
item.description: LyricsNow is a free app that shows lyrics line by line in time with your music, for songs from Apple Music or a connected Spotify account. It was #97 among free apps on the US Mac App Store on 15 November.

item.title: MyMediCompass app keeps track of doctor appointments and copays
item.description: MyMediCompass is a new iPhone app for people who see several doctors: it ties each visit to its copay, notes and prescriptions, and gathers what happened at other doctors before your next appointment. It was #91 in Health & Fitness on the US App Store's top paid chart on 15 November.

item.title: Pinu Club is a free AI language learning app with speaking feedback
item.description: Pinu Club is a new iPhone app for learning a language in short lessons, with AI feedback on your pronunciation as you speak words and sentences. It was #88 in Education on the US App Store's free chart on 15 November.

item.title: Platen typewriter app for iPhone brings paper, ink and key sounds
item.description: Platen — Paper & Ink is a writing app that makes your iPhone feel like a typewriter, with textured paper, uneven ink and mechanical sounds. It was #77 in Productivity on the US App Store's free chart on 15 November.

item.title: PlayerMap GPS app with CarPlay redraws your streets like a video game
item.description: PlayerMap is a new iPhone navigation app that shows real roads and addresses in video-game styles, such as a neon night city or a fantasy atlas, with turn-by-turn voice directions. It was #71 in Navigation on the US App Store's free chart on 15 November.

item.title: Pocket Classic turns your iPhone into an iPod-style music player
item.description: Pocket Classic is a 99-cent app that lets you browse your Apple Music library with an on-screen click wheel and a cover carousel. It was #57 among paid Music apps on the US App Store on 15 November, a day after it came out.

item.title: Remindly notes app: any note can carry a reminder, on iPhone and Mac
item.description: Remindly is a new notes app where a note can remind you once, on repeat, all day or when you arrive somewhere; it launched on Product Hunt on 15 November. It's free on two devices, and Pro costs $49 a year or $5.99 a month.

item.title: Samsung Quick Measure and AR Doodle apps discontinued on December 31
item.description: Samsung is pulling its Quick Measure and AR Doodle apps for Galaxy phones from the Galaxy Store on December 31, 2026. After that date there are no new downloads and no more updates.

item.title: ScreenRecess screen time app for iPhone pauses a group of apps
item.description: ScreenRecess is a new $4.99 iPhone and iPad app that gives a group of apps one shared time allowance, then locks them for a break. It was #62 in Productivity among paid apps on the US App Store on 15 November.

item.title: SkyWX free weather radar app with severe weather alerts
item.description: SkyWX is a new free weather app with US radar, forecasts and severe weather alerts, made by former St. Louis TV meteorologist Anthony Slaughter. It was #68 in Weather among free apps on the US App Store on 15 November.

item.title: Smart glasses privacy concerns: how Google's new glasses handle them
item.description: Google's Gemini glasses, on pre-order since 12 November, turn on an outside light when they take a photo or video, are designed to block the camera if that light is covered, and blur bystanders' faces before images go to Gemini; Google calls these design measures, and no independent tests have been published yet.

item.title: TidyMap neighborhood map app colors in the city areas you've visited
item.description: TidyMap is a new $3.99 iPhone and iPad app that splits a city into neighborhoods and colors in each one you mark as visited, lived in or want to go. It was #61 among paid Travel apps on the US App Store on 15 November.

item.title: Tripmo AI group trip planner lets each friend plan through ChatGPT or Claude
item.description: Tripmo is a new shared trip plan that each person in a group fills in by talking to their own AI, such as ChatGPT, Claude or Grok. Places, flights and bookings land in one plan on a map, sorted by day.

item.title: AT&T landline shutdown starts November 15, Verizon copper on November 16
item.description: AT&T is allowed to start shutting off old copper landlines in parts of 18 US states from November 15, and Verizon starts similar steps in 8 states on November 16. DSL internet over the same copper lines is being retired too.

item.title: Beaver PDF scanner app for iPhone, iPad and Mac keeps scans offline
item.description: Beaver is a new PDF scanner app for iPhone, iPad and Mac that does everything on your device: no account, no upload and no tracking. It costs $1.99 on the App Store, and its code is open source.

item.title: ChartMe chore chart app for kids: points, streaks and rewards
item.description: ChartMe is a new family chore chart for iPhone and iPad where kids tick off chores on their own device, earn points and spend them on rewards parents set up. It was #74 in Productivity on the US App Store's paid chart on November 14.

item.title: ChatGPT shopping answers can point to fake online stores, study says
item.description: About 9% of 6,795 shopping answers from ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity named fake, suspicious or dead shopping sites, a study by US brand-protection firm Podqi found. Perplexity did so in 15% of its answers, ChatGPT in 8% and Gemini in 4%.

item.title: Clackity flip clock app turns the iPhone Duo into a desk clock
item.description: Clackity is a new split-flap clock app that looks and sounds like an old train station departure board, made for the iPhone Duo and working on any iPhone. It was #7 in Utilities on the US App Store's paid chart on November 14.

item.title: Clyper AI clip maker turns long videos into vertical Shorts and Reels
item.description: Clyper is a new AI clip maker on the web: paste a YouTube, Twitch, Google Drive or Dropbox link, or upload a file, and it cuts the video into vertical 9:16 clips with word-by-word captions. Paid plans start at 19 dollars a month.

item.title: Color Jar color picker app for iPhone saves colors from camera or photos
item.description: Color Jar is a new color picker app that grabs a color from your camera, a photo or a screenshot and saves it with a name, ready to copy as hex, rgb or hsl. It costs 4.99 dollars once and was #27 among paid Graphics & Design apps on the US App Store on November 14.

item.title: CrowCards flashcard app with no subscription and no account
item.description: CrowCards is a flashcard app for iPhone and iPad that you buy once for 3.99 dollars: no account, no login and no subscription. It was #30 among paid Education apps on the US App Store on November 14.

item.title: Digital home key and car key on your phone: how they work now
item.description: Your phone's wallet app can now hold keys for compatible front doors, cars and hotel rooms, and since 11 November Google Wallet holds home keys too, using Aliro, a smart lock standard backed by Apple, Google and Samsung.

item.title: FullSky 3D weather radar app lets you slice through US storms
item.description: FullSky shows live US weather radar in 3D, so you can turn a storm around and cut through it to see hail cores or signs of rotation. It costs 4.99 dollars and was #30 among paid Weather apps on the US App Store on November 14.

item.title: Google Family Hub comes to Pixel Settings for family plans and location
item.description: Pixel phones now show a Family section near the top of Settings that puts a Google family group's members, shared Google One storage, Play Family Library, shared payments and live location in one place. 9to5Google says it appeared widely on Pixels by 14 November.
